import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 274

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/274](https://www.erdosproblems.com/274)
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)
* [arXiv:1803.08301](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08301)
* [arXiv:1803.03569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03569)
* [PMC7247885](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7247885/)
* [arXiv:1804.11103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11103)
-/

open scoped Pointwise Cardinal

namespace Erdos274

-- TODO(callesonne): add already proved results from the wiki page

/-- An exact covering of a group `G` is a finite collection of subgroups `{H_1, ..., H_k}` and
representative `{g_1, ..., g_k}` such that the cosets `g_iH_i` are pairwise disjoint and their
union covers `G`.

Note that this differs from `Partition (α := Subgroup G)` because the covering condition there
invokes `Subgroup.sup` which is subgroup generation and thus stronger than union. This definition
is easier to use in this context than the alternative `Partition (α := Set G)`, which lacks
subgroup definitions such as `Subgroup.index`. -/
structure Group.ExactCovering (G : Type*) [Group G] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] where
  parts : ι → Subgroup G
  reps : ι → G
  nonempty (i : ι) : (parts i : Set G).Nonempty
  disjoint : (Set.univ (α := ι)).PairwiseDisjoint fun (i : ι) ↦ reps i • (parts i : Set G)
  covers : ⋃ i, reps i • (parts i : Set G) = Set.univ

/--
If $G$ is a group, can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one coset
of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets.)

The conjectured answer is no: in every such exact covering, two of the subgroups have
the same cardinality.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem erdos_274 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G],
    1 < ENat.card G → ∀ (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι],
    ∀ (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι), 1 < Fintype.card ι →
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j) := by
  sorry

/--
If `G` is a finite abelian group then there cannot exist an exact covering of `G` by more
than one cosets of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one
of the cosets.)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jostamon/erdos274-hs-abelian/blob/2ab8a2e39e7dd7836adf577b52555f069244466f/Erdos274/Main.lean"]
theorem erdos_274.variants.abelian {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [CommGroup G]
    (hG : 1 < Fintype.card G) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι)
    (hι : 1 < Fintype.card ι) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $G$ be a group, and let $A = \{a_1G_1, \dots, a_kG_k\}$ be a finite system of left cosets of
subgroups $G_1, \dots, G_k$ of $G$.

Herzog and Schönheim conjectured that if $A$ forms a partition of $G$ with $k > 1$, then the
indices $[G:G_1], \dots, [G:G_k]$ cannot be distinct.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem herzog_schonheim {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : 1 < ENat.card G) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (hι : 1 < Fintype.card ι) (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index := by
  sorry

end Erdos274

findings.description: The yes/no answer is reversed. At lines 60–63, `answer(sorry)` is equivalent to the assertion that every admissible exact covering contains two equal-sized subgroups. Let E be the existence of an exact covering with more than one coset and pairwise distinct coset cardinalities—the source's question. The current RHS is equivalent to ¬E, not E: translating a subgroup preserves cardinality, and the extra nontriviality bound on G is redundant. Consequently `answer(True)` would mean that no such covering exists, while `answer(False)` would mean that one exists. This reversal was verified without sorry in `/workspace/review/polarity.lean`, including a proof that the two interpretations cannot agree for the same answer proposition.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/274, with exact wording at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/274: “If $G$ is a group then can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one cosets of different sizes?” The source also explicitly says that for abelian G “the answer to the original question is no.” These pages were read through the public Jina reader after direct requests encountered Cloudflare challenges.
findings.suggested_fix: Negate the entire current universal RHS: `answer(sorry) ↔ ¬ (∀ (G : Type*) [Group G], 1 < ENat.card G → ∀ (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι], ∀ (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι), 1 < Fintype.card ι → ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j))`. Equivalently, state existence of an admissible covering whose subgroup-cardinality function is injective. Retain the unknown answer and open status.

reformulations.difference: Lean adds `1 < ENat.card G` and uses the natural-valued `Subgroup.index` without explicitly assuming finite indices, whereas the sources describe a nontrivial coset partition with finite indices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both apparent hypothesis differences are harmless. Representatives of distinct parts are distinct, so more than one disjoint coset forces G to be nontrivial. Neumann's finite coset-cover theorem permits deleting all infinite-index cosets without destroying a cover. In an exact covering every coset is nonempty and indispensable, so every subgroup must have finite index. Thus the default value zero of `Subgroup.index` is unreachable. These implications and the equivalences for adding or removing the hypotheses were proved in `/workspace/review/cover_checks.lean`.

reformulations.difference: The variant restricts G to finite abelian groups and asserts equal subgroup cardinalities; the Erdős source gives nonexistence for abelian groups without a finiteness restriction, and the Herzog–Schönheim formulation uses equal indices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Each coset is bijective with its subgroup. For finite G, Lagrange's identity `|H| [G:H] = |G|`, with positive factors, makes equal subgroup cardinalities equivalent to equal indices. For infinite G, every subgroup in a finite exact covering has finite index and therefore cardinality |G|, so the cardinality conclusion is automatic when there are at least two parts. Consequently the finite-abelian cardinality statement is equivalent to the unrestricted abelian cardinality statement. The extra bound on |G| also follows from the covering. The global finite-abelian reduction and the cardinality/index and coset/subgroup equivalences were proved in `/workspace/review/cover_checks.lean`.

review.notes: All four declared objects were reviewed. Apart from the main answer-slot polarity, no mathematical defect was found. ExactCovering was proved equivalent to unique coset membership. Boundary checks excluded empty index types and nontrivial coverings of a trivial group, constructed one-part covers and an order-two singleton cover, and evaluated its subgroup sizes as [(0, 1), (1, 1)]. The scratch files compile, and the verification lemmas do not depend on sorryAx. The sources retain the general open status and confirm the solved abelian case. The cited external Lean proof has the matching mathematical statement and covering definition; its project was inspected but not rebuilt. All experiments are under /workspace/review, and the reviewed file remains unchanged.

submission.summary: Negated the entire universal right-hand side so that the answer slot now represents existence of a distinct-size exact covering, as the source asks. Preserved the unknown answer, open status, docstring, and all other declarations. The required Lean compile command succeeds with only the permitted `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
